answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-sequential compute-proof-work per identity to act as a resilient gateway for the network. The verifier enforces this by checking if every hash output matches a unique, ephemeral task, treating each identity like a ferrous core that must be magnetized by raw energy. While an honest agent pays this base cost once, an attacker attempting to build a copper circuit for 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, effectively falling into a deep canyon of processing exhaustion.
